builds.name: Reference: Ranked mid core
builds.goal: Reference for Mel: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ mid players use most (4,062 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 46.8% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A repeated-hit mage who accumulates Overwhelm, uses a root zone to maintain hits and times Rebuttal against projectiles. The current mid provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Luden's Echo → Shadowflame → Zhonya's Hourglass. Arcane Comet keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Sorcerer's Shoes, Rabadon's Deathcap, Void Staff.
builds.summary: The proven mid baseline: Luden's Echo → Shadowflame → Zhonya's Hourglass, with Arcane Comet.
testPlan: Play it in mid as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Luden's Echo → Shadowflame → Zhonya's Hourglass) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 46.8% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Luden's Echo → Shadowflame → Zhonya's Hourglass.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.

Mel forms a barrier around herself that reflects projectiles from enemy champions, gaining [80 / 110 / 140 / 170 / 200 + (0.7) × AP] Shields for [0.75] seconds and [40]% decaying Move Speed for [0.75] seconds.

Reflected projectiles deal [0.4 / 0.45 / 0.5 / 0.55 / 0.6 + (0.0005) × AP] original damage as magic damage.

When applied, if the stored amount exceeds the enemy's combined shields and Health, they are executed.

When an Ability is cast, Mel's next Attack fires [3] extra projectiles, each dealing [characterLevelInterpolation(8 → 30; raw flags preserved) + (0.04) × AP] magic damage. This effect can stack up to [9] extra projectiles.

Active: Mel unleashes her power on all enemies affected by Overwhelm, dealing [125 / 200 / 275 + (0.3) × AP] magic damage plus [4 / 7 / 10 + (0.04) × AP] magic damage per Overwhelm stack.

Can only be cast when an enemy champion is affected by Overwhelm.

Mel unleashes a barrage of [6 / 7 / 8 / 9 / 10] projectiles that explode in the area around a target location.

Mel fires a radiating orb, Rooting enemies at its center for [1.5] seconds and dealing [60 / 105 / 150 / 195 / 240 + (0.7) × AP] magic damage.

The orb builds up a hostile area around it that Slows enemies by [30]% and deals [16 / 28 / 40 / 52 / 64 + (0.08) × AP] magic damage per second.

builds.name: Brilliance attack weaver
builds.summary: Convert stored post-cast projectiles into a real attack burst.
builds.goal: Convert stored post-cast projectiles into a real attack burst.
builds.hypothesis: Searing Brilliance grants three extra projectiles after an ability, stored up to nine, each with 0.04 AP magic damage. Nashor and Dusk and Dawn reward the actual releasing attack while Cosmic Drive assists positioning. Q/E multi-hit magic damage builds five-second Overwhelm stacks for R, so attack weaving tests additional stack delivery rather than replacing spells entirely.
testPlan: Required state: Need stored projectiles, a tagged champion and a safe attack before stacks expire.
Count extra projectiles, Overwhelm stacks and item procs for one versus three stored casts.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Holding all projectiles can waste short Overwhelm windows; attacking exposes Mel after W's 0.75-second protection.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Extra projectiles are not automatically nine full Nashor or Spellblade applications.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Nashor's Tooth, Dusk and Dawn, Cosmic Drive, Rabadon's Deathcap, Cryptbloom, Sorcerer's Shoes. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Survive the engage
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Mel: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A repeated-hit mage who accumulates Overwhelm, uses a root zone to maintain hits and times Rebuttal against projectiles. Record Overwhelm stacks and reflected projectile type. A reflected spell is not arbitrary opponent damage you can always choose; compare real attacks/passive bolts separately. A transformed mana shield, stasis and a spell shield may preserve repeat casts.
builds.summary: A transformed mana shield, stasis and a spell shield may preserve repeat casts.
testPlan: Kit question for Mel: Record Overwhelm stacks and reflected projectile type. A reflected spell is not arbitrary opponent damage you can always choose; compare real attacks/passive bolts separately.

Start with the early core (Archangel, then the defense matching the opponent) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: A transformed mana shield, stasis and a spell shield may preserve repeat casts. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Mel fires a barrage of projectiles that explode around a target location, dealing damage repeatedly to enemies within the area. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Defensive redundancy can sacrifice too much damage; this is conditional on real threats.

The route fails Mel's stated kit question: Record Overwhelm stacks and reflected projectile type. A reflected spell is not arbitrary opponent damage you can always choose; compare real attacks/passive bolts separately.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: Defensive redundancy can sacrifice too much damage; this is conditional on real threats.
Full cost 16,000 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Archangel, then the defense matching the opponent. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Banshee's Veil, Rylai's Crystal Scepter, Void Staff are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Reflective AP shield counter
builds.summary: Make reflected projectile windows useful against projectile-heavy teams.
builds.goal: Make reflected projectile windows useful against projectile-heavy teams.
builds.hypothesis: Rebuttal shields with 0.7 AP for 0.75 seconds and returns a rank/AP fraction of original projectile damage as magic. Visage strengthens the received shield, Rod supplies mana/health and Deathcap supports both shield and reflect coefficient. E's center root can trigger Aftershock defenses before a dangerous reflect, while Bloodletter relies on actual spell magic hits.
testPlan: Required state: Need an incoming reflectable projectile, W timing and E center root rather than only the slow area.
Compare shield absorbed and reflected magic damage across small and large projectiles, recording original damage.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Non-projectile attacks bypass reflection; mistiming the tiny window leaves a low-burst defensive build.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Reflection does not guarantee original damage type, all spell effects or an ability's complete return payload.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Rod of Ages, Spirit Visage, Rabadon's Deathcap, Bloodletter's Curse, Zhonya's Hourglass, Mercury's Treads. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
